transcript.text: hotpoint SA2 oven not heatin on fan, grill ok. wat does SA2 mean??

“SA2” is usually the Hotpoint oven model series/range, not an error code. For example, models may be called something like SA2 540 H IX. The full model and service number are normally on a label around the oven door frame.

If the grill heats normally but fan-oven mode does not, the most common cause is a failed fan oven heating element (the circular element at the back, behind the fan cover).

Quick clues:

• Fan runs but oven stays cold: very likely fan element, its wiring, or the fan-function switch/relay.
• Fan does not run and no heat: could be the fan motor, selector switch, thermostat/control board, or wiring.
• It heats on another oven setting but not fan oven: again points strongly to the fan element/circuit.
• Make sure you have not selected a fan-only/defrost setting — that setting runs the fan with no heat by design.

Because this is mains electrical work, switch power off at the cooker isolator before removing any panels. A replacement fan element is often a straightforward repair for an appliance engineer, but the exact part depends on the full model/service number.
thx. the fan at the back doesnt spin tho, just a low hum from back. was noisy for few weeks b4 that. whats it likely to be then?

That sounds most likely like a failing/seized fan motor rather than the heating element.

The sequence of:

1. Fan getting noisy for weeks
2. Now only a low hum
3. Fan not turning

is typical of worn motor bearings or a motor that has jammed. The motor is getting power and trying to start (the hum), but cannot rotate.

Possible causes, in likelihood order:

• Fan motor bearings worn/seized — most likely.
• Something physically catching the fan blade — grease/debris, loose panel, or warped blade. With power isolated, check whether the fan blade turns freely by hand.
• Motor capacitor — some fan motors use one; a failed capacitor can cause humming/no starting. Many oven fan motors are shaded-pole types and do not have a separate replaceable capacitor, though.
• Control/selector fault — less likely if it hums, because it suggests power is reaching the motor.

Do not keep running it while it hums: it can overheat the motor and potentially damage the control circuit. Turn it off at the cooker isolator.

An engineer would normally replace the fan motor, and often inspect/replace the fan blade and rear element at the same time. Get the full model/service number from the sticker around the door opening before ordering parts — ��SA2” alone is not enough.
ok isolated it at the cooker switch n tried the fan blade by hand, its very stiff n feels gritty. model on the plate inside the door frame is SA2 540 H IX

That confirms it pretty strongly: the oven fan motor bearings have failed/seized. The gritty, stiff feel is not normal — the blade should turn smoothly and fairly freely by hand.

For a Hotpoint SA2 540 H IX, you will likely need the fan oven motor (sometimes sold with/without the rear fan blade). Check the exact service code / commercial code too, usually on the same rating plate, before buying, as Hotpoint parts can vary by production version.

What to do:

• Keep it isolated; don’t run it humming or try to force it.
• Replacement normally involves removing the rear internal fan cover and blade, then accessing the motor from the rear of the oven.
• The fan-blade retaining nut may be a left-hand thread on many ovens — meaning it may undo clockwise. Check the service information/part instructions for your specific motor before applying force.
• Given the oven’s age/use, inspect the circular fan heating element while the cover is off. If it is visibly burnt, split, or has blown, replace that too — but the seized motor definitely needs attention first.

If you are comfortable removing an integrated oven and working around mains wiring, it is often a manageable repair. Otherwise, tell an appliance engineer: “Hotpoint SA2 540 H IX; fan motor hums, blade is stiff/gritty and won’t spin; grill works.” That should point them directly to the fan motor.
